Wigan Council leader Nazia Rehman said Sir Billy was "more than a sporting legend, he was a pioneer, an inspiration, and someone who brought immense pride to Wigan Borough". Image caption, The statue of Sir Billy Boston in Believe Square, Wigan, was unveiled in 2016 Rehman said: "Following his passing, we wanted to ensure his legacy continues to be honoured in the heart of our town. "That's why we are renaming Believe Square, the home of Sir Billy's statue, as Sir Billy Boston Square." Thomas White, 43, was given an Imprisonment for Public Protection (IPP) sentence for stealing a mobile phone in 2012. The Ministry of Justice has been approached for comment. Clara said the family "felt a small sense of hope" when White was moved from HMP Manchester to a secure psychiatric hospital, but now say "he is being sent back into the very system that made him ill". She said her brother, who has a teenage son, had already been moved between 14 prisons and that this latest transfer would make it his 15th in 14 years. While he needed treatment and support, he was instead being "sent back to prison with no release date and no certainty about what his future holds", she said. White had been binge-drinking in Manchester before he stole a phone from two Christian missionaries in 2012. He was given an IPP sentence with a minimum tariff of two years. His family said he has now spent more than 14 years in custody, serving more than seven times that period. title: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme

input.lead: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
input.summary: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
input.evidence_text: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme - BBC News Image caption, The CyanLines project will see a number of "floating walkways" connecting different parts of Manchester By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 10 September 2026 Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed. It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade. The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme. Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others. Pete Bradshaw, director of sustainability at Manchester City, said: "The plans for the CyanLines route add a new layer of nature-rich, innovative and imaginative active travel and community experiences for fans, visitors and those living and working in the neighbourhood." Image caption, The next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct park project has also been announced Funding for the next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct "garden in the sky" was also announced. Part of the old railway line has been transformed into a public park, which opened in 2022.

input.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. input.evidence_text: And in the years that followed, several much-loved bars, restaurants and nightclubs have called the building home, but many have departed. As Stephen Topping reports , both the Tiger Tiger nightclub and the Waxy O'Connor's Irish pub were open for almost 20 years before they close New openings in the old Tiger Tiger unit proved to be short-lived - and it now sits side-by-side with the former Hard Rock Cafe, which closed for the final time earlier this year. Chiquito, Bierkeller and O'Neills have also closed their doors in the last year "If a place gets a reputation for being dead, it just hastens the decline of it," said veteran councillor Pat Karney. So what’s going on with this iconic city centre venue? View 6 Images The Hard Rock Cafe sign remains on Printworks - but the restaurant has been shut for months (Image: Manchester Evening News) It's understood that Manchester council's economic team met with Printworks bosses earlier this year to discuss future plans. Challenging trading conditions, the cost of living crisis and changing customer trends were all discussed It's believed Printworks bosses are now shifting focus towards the site being a more community-focused, family-friendly venue, and further discussions will take place with the council
